request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now sign in by typing a name and load a sheet by typing its id, all on the one screen at `/`. The acceptance test passes under `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:**
- **Sign-in:** typing a name and pressing sign-in shows that name in `current-user`. There's no password. The name is kept in the page address (the `user` parameter), as DESIGN.md says to do for screen state. There's also a sign-out button.
- **Loading a sheet:** typing an id and pressing load asks the server for that sheet through a new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}` endpoint. When the answer comes back, the id shows in `sheet-current-id`. The id is kept in the page address too (the `sheet` parameter). Loading always fetches the sheet from the server again, even if it was loaded before, so you see what another user has changed.
- **Never-loaded sheets:** the server accepts any id, and an id never used before comes back as an empty sheet.
- **Errors:** an empty name or an empty sheet id shows an error (`signin-error` / `sheet-error`). The error clears as soon as you type in that field again.
- **Room for later features:** I added a slot called `sheet.panel` that appears inside the loaded sheet. Future per-sheet features can put their panels there without changing this screen.

**Limits to know about:**
- **Nothing is stored yet.** A sheet is just its id: there's no database table and no audit record, because a sheet has nothing in it yet. The first feature that adds per-sheet data will need to add the table.
- **The server doesn't know who is signed in.** The name exists only in the browser. Later changes that need `by=<user>` in the audit file will have to send it with each request.
- **Old placeholder kept:** the "Nothing here yet." text (`home-empty`) used to be the whole home page. It now shows inside a loaded sheet while nothing fills the slot, because AGENTS.md says test ids must never be removed.

The new code is in `features/session/`, `features/sheet/`, `slots/defs/sheetPanel.ts` and `routes/index.tsx` on the front end. On the server it's `sheet/` under `net/officefloor/hq/app` plus `officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}.GET.yml`.
